source.title: Circuits in Superposition: Compressing many small neural networks into one

record.file_problem: The full post is present. It includes a later edit saying some of the mathematics was wrong, though the authors say the high-level conceptual takeaways are largely unchanged.
record.tranche_reason: The post gives a theoretical construction for superposing computations and explicitly argues that superposition need not consist of one-dimensional features. This refines the geometry claim, but it does not test learned feature representations in actual models.
record.gate_note: The construction and error analysis bear on superposition and its geometry. The parameter-count result and interference bound are recorded as findings not covered by the listed versions. The post does not measure learned features, polysemantic neurons, or LLM representations.
record.test_reason: A theoretical construction, with no trained models, showing that many small networks can be superposed into one larger network as random d-dimensional subspaces rather than 1-D directions. This is a specific argument bearing on V6. It is an expressivity or existence result only, and no learned representations are measured.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also stress that capacity scales with parameters rather than neurons, that there is 'no superposition in parameter space', and that circuits may be cross-layer. They also say the parameter vector may decompose into per-subnetwork sums. All of this is offered as tentative, 'with a heavy pinch of salt', since real networks may differ.
record.recipe_differences: The post develops a theoretical construction for computing small neural networks in superposition, rather than reproducing the original toy-model feature-learning setup.
record.method_sensitivity: The construction's error and parameter bounds depend on the number k of simultaneously active subnetworks and on the widths M and D; the post assumes subnetworks have a stated degree of noise robustness.

fits_no_version.finding: The number of superposable small networks scales with total parameter count (N≈Õ(kTn)), not neuron count, and read-in interference dominates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Computation in superposition is bounded by parameter count, i.e. there is no superposition in parameter space, with interference set by the number of active subnetworks and by widths M and D.

fits_no_version.finding: The authors argue that circuits need not follow layer structure, producing 'cross-layer superposition'. This is an argument only, with no rows.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Superposed circuits can span multiple layers, so single-layer activations may look like half-computed nonsense.

record.problems: The evidence is theoretical rather than empirical and assumes small networks are robust to a specified amount of noise. The post itself notes that real networks may use different constructions and that correlations between circuits are not addressed. A later edit says some of the mathematics was wrong; comments in the post also raise a concern about compounding noise across layers.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results relevant to the listed versions were reported. The post's discussion of chaining subnetworks and possible real-world implications is not an empirical test.

untested.parts: Learned toy-model geometry, the sparsity-dependent phase transition and regular geometry. The near-orthogonal subspaces here are built by hand, not learned.
Whether polysemanticity arises from capacity competition, and importance-based allocation of dimensions.
Any LLM neuron-spread or SAE evidence.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable or canonical.
Whether trained networks actually superpose multi-dimensional subspaces or 1-D directions. The authors flag training dynamics as future work.

missing.what: The 'no superposition in parameter space' implication: the network cannot implement more distinct operations than its parameter dimension.

record.verdict_notes: This is a purely theoretical Alignment Forum post. The 12.08.2025 edit says some of the maths was wrong, and a fixed version exists in a follow-up post. A commenter (Linsefors) reports noise compounding across layers in this embedding. Verdicts should be read as being about expressivity, not about what networks learn.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test whether learned toy-model features are stored as nearly orthogonal directions, a sparsity-dependent transition, or regular feature geometry.
Does not test whether neuron polysemanticity results from competition for capacity, or whether feature importance determines dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Does not study polysemantic neurons or alternative causes of polysemanticity.
Does not study LLM representations, neuron-spread measures, or SAE recovery.
Does not assess whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical.
The construction is theoretical; it does not establish what representations are learned in real networks.

rows.subject: constructed large residual network
rows.size_stated: Residual width D≫d and MLP width M≫m; T small networks, each with residual width d and m neurons per layer.
rows.operation_detail: Constructs a superposition of small networks using random projections into the large network's residual stream.
rows.measure: Dimensionality and form of the superposed representations
rows.value: Each small network is embedded in a random d-dimensional subspace of the D-dimensional residual stream; the post says computation in superposition does not require one-dimensional variables, and the circuits' internal representations need not be sparse or linear.
rows.locator: Introduction, “Some very tentative implications, maybe?”; The Construction
rows.note: This is a theoretical construction, not a measurement of representations learned by trained models.
rows.check: Reversed only inside the hand-built construction: each subnetwork occupies a random d-dim subspace, not 1-D directions. It is not a measurement of learned features, so it shows possibility, not that real networks do this. The later erratum and a comment about noise compounding across layers weaken the multi-layer proof.

source_check.correct: state=cannot_determine: the construction permits subnetworks with arbitrary internal representations in d-dimensional subspaces; it does not establish that superposed features are irreducibly multidimensional.

source_check.problem: Embedding entire subnetworks in d-dimensional subspaces and dispensing with a one-dimensional-feature assumption does not demonstrate the opposite of V6.
